data.name: Candie
data.gender_notes: Candie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old French word ‘Candide’, meaning ‘sweet’ or ‘delightful’. In the novel by Voltaire, Candide is an optimistic hero who learns that the world is not perfect but that one should remain hopeful and steadfast in the face of adversity. The name Candie carries the meaning “Sweet or Delightful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Candie usually hope their child will grow to embody sweet or delightful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the sweetness and delight of spiritual growth and faith.
data.etymology: Candie belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sweet or Delightful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Candie total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: קנדי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קנדי מקורו בשם העברי קנדידה, שפירושו מתוקה, ניקרא. הוא קשור למונח קנד, שפירושו להיות לבן, זך. השם מופיע בכתבי הקודש ככינוי לאהבה אלוהית.

in_greek.name: Κάνδη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κάνδη προέρχεται από το λατινικό Candida, που σημαίνει λευκή, αγνή. Η λέξη συνδέεται με την ελληνική λέξη κανδή, που σημαίνει καινούργια και καθαρή. Στην παράδοση των Πατέρων της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα σχετίζεται με την πνευματική αγνότητα.

in_latin.name: Candida
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Candida originates from the Latin word candidus, meaning white, shining. It was used to describe someone with a pure and chaste character. In early Christian tradition, the name symbolized spiritual purity and moral integrity.

in_english.name: Candie
in_english.long_meaning: The name Candie is derived from the Latin Candida, meaning white, pure. It has roots in Hebrew and Greek traditions, symbolizing sweetness, innocence, and spiritual purity. Historically, the name has been associated with virtues of moral integrity and compassion in Christian cultures.
